title: Usage classification, entitlement exactness, and invoice mapping for mixed-model requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for mapping fine-grained usage classes to plan entitlements and producing deterministic invoice line-items for requests that touch multiple pricing dimensions (model family, API surface, priority pool). Motivation: Customers running production LLM features mix interactive completion calls, high-volume embedding batches, and occasional high-cost reranking requests. Current billing produces opaque invoices when a single client request triggers multiple internal model variants or falls back to lower-cost models. We need a clear contract so customers and finance can reconcile spend to features and SLOs.

Scope: - Define canonical "usage classification" categories (interactive, streaming, embeddings, batch-embed, rerank) and tag rules for mixed requests. - Specify entitlement exactness: each plan must declare quotas by classification and by model weight class (small/medium/large); entitlement checks must be deterministic and logged. - Define invoice mapping rules so a single multi-part request yields predictable line-items (either atomic consolidated line or multiple line-items with clear grouping). - Acceptance criteria include API-level headers, logs, and invoice formatting.

Out of scope: pricing math changes, UI billing portal redesign (separate tickets).
goals: Provide deterministic mapping from request -> billing tag(s) such that identical requests always produce the same invoice line semantics
Ensure plan entitlements can be expressed and enforced by classification and model weight bands
Produce invoice line-items that are human-readable, taggable, and reconcile to usage exports and per-route metrics
success_metrics: >99.9% of invoices for contested customers reconcile without manual adjustments in first 30 days
Support team reduction in billing dispute response time from median 48h to <8h for affected customers
Billing export contains a billing_tag for every token/embedding unit with no nulls
requirements: 1) Define canonical usage classifications and exact tagging rules for request payloads (see API examples below)
2) Entitlement model: plans must be able to declare quotas by classification and by model weight band (e.g., embeddings-small: 10M units/month)
3) Enforcement modes: soft (notifications + provisional billing) and hard (deny with 402/overage path or 429 rate-limit) configurable per plan

4) Multi-segment requests: clear rule for either (A) atomically aggregate to the highest-cost classification for single line-item OR (B) emit multiple line-items per segment with a grouping_id in invoices; both behaviors must be supported via per-customer preference flag
5) Billing tags: every request must emit a billing_tag header and log field that contains classification:model_family:model_weight:plan_id (e.g., interactive:gpt-4:large:plan-1234)
6) For fallback events (runtime substitution to lower-cost model), logs must include both requested_billing_tag and actual_billing_tag and a reason code for fallback
7) Invoice export schema must include grouping_id, billing_tag, units, unit_price, subtotal, currency, and source_request_id
8) Proration rules for plan changes mid-cycle: prorated entitlements and invoice lines should be grouped by effective_date and include prior_plan_id and new_plan_id fields
9) Auditability: ability to reconstruct per-request charges from raw logs plus pricing tables within 14 days for any invoice line
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Canonical classifications documented and reviewed by billing, finance, PM, and eng. Document includes examples and decision log (doc link in links).

AC-2: For a synthetic test payload that interleaves a 50-token completion + 100 embedding vectors + a rerank call, system produces either a single invoice line at configured consolidation mode or three lines with same grouping_id when grouping mode is enabled. Automated test verifies line semantics.

AC-3: All requests emitted in production sample stream include a non-empty billing_tag header and matching billing_tag in billing export. Spot-check script validates 10k sample records with zero null billing_tags.

AC-4: When a request is transparently downgraded from requested model (e.g., gpt-4-large -> gpt-4-small), logs include requested_billing_tag, actual_billing_tag, and fallback_reason. Billing exports apply the actual_billing_tag price. Finance verifies one sample invoice where fallback occurred matches exported charges.

AC-5: Entitlement enforcement modes: when a plan hits soft quota, customer receives webhook notification and provisional invoice line flagged 'soft_overage' but requests are allowed. When plan hits hard quota, requests are rejected with HTTP 402 and error code 'quota_exceeded' and no billing lines are created. Tests for both modes pass against staging with plan toggles.

AC-6: Proration behavior validated: simulate plan change on 2025-04-12 for customer X; invoice for April shows grouped lines with prior_plan_id and new_plan_id and prorated entitlements. Finance confirms amounts align with expected proration calculator within ±0.5%.
AC-7: Performance: adding billing_tag generation and entitlement checks must add <2ms P50 and <10ms P99 latency to existing request path in staging (measured with 1k concurrent synthetic clients).

AC-8: Backfill safety: when rolling this into production, existing invoice exports remain stable. A pilot customer (account-375) runs in 'grouping' mode for 2 weeks with no manual adjustments reported.
implementation_notes: ENG work: entitlement API (read-only fast-path) must be cached with TTL 30s and support 10k rps
Add billing_tag header to public API and ensure SDKs surface it in responses (SDK PRs needed)
Add grouping_id to internal request context used by billing pipeline and invoice builder
Pricing service to expose pricing lookup by billing_tag; make sure metric cardinality is bounded by model_family + weight band + plan_id
Create migration plan for legacy invoices; produce compatibility layer that maps old line-item types to new billing_tag semantics for 6 months
api_contract_examples: Invoice CSV line example: grouping_id, billing_tag, source_request_id, units, unit_price, subtotal, currency => gid-20250412-abc,interactive:gpt-4:large:plan-1234,req-789,50,0.0200,1.00,USD
